title: Adaptive layerwise WO INT8 profile integration + canary regression harness for GPTQ/AWQ
creator: Marco Liu
description:
Goal: Integrate per-layer adaptive weight-only (WO) INT8 profiles produced by both GPTQ and AWQ toolchains into our inference runtime, and build a canary + smoke regression harness that validates accuracy, latency, and stability across representative workloads. This ticket scopes the integration glue, a deterministic calibration workflow, golden prompt sets, automated divergence detection, and an orchestration plan for rolling canaries and automated rollbacks.

Motivation: Recent AWQ/GPTQ outputs show variable layer sensitivity — a coarse global scale causes unacceptable drift for some models and prompt classes. A layer-adaptive profile reduces quality regressions while preserving the latency/cost benefits of WO INT8. We need: deterministic calibration, cross-toolchain parity checks, and a reliable regression gate that can be used in CI and production canaries.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Runtime can consume per-layer profile artifacts (GPTQ and AWQ formats) and map them to kernel dispatch without manual conversion.
2) Calibration workflow produces deterministic profile artifacts given the same seed, dataset slice, and model version.
3) Canary harness runs against a baseline FP32 run and flags regressions when any configured metric exceeds threshold.
4) Regression thresholds defined and codified: embedding cosine drop > 0.015 average OR generation KL > 0.02 OR top-1 token mismatch > 3% for golden set -> fail.
5) Smoke suite completes within 15 minutes for the nightly subset and reports to the console dashboard and PR comments.
6) Automated rollback playbook exercised with a staged canary and validated in the staging cluster.
implementation_notes:
- Add a profile loader that supports: GPTQ JSON weight metadata, AWQ per-layer scale tensors, and a compact mapping file for kernel choices.
- Implement layer-sensitivity masks: allow certain layers to fall back to 16-bit or FP16 if quantization causes > threshold divergence during local calibration.
- Calibration harness should: sample N=500 representative prompts (stratified by length & domain), run deterministic PRNG seed, collect per-layer quantization error histograms, and write a compact artifact with seed+dataset-hash for reproducibility.
- Store artifacts in s3://redwood-quant-profiles/{model}/{version}/{toolchain}/{seed}-{dataset-hash}.profile
- Add config flags to runtime: --profile-path, --fallback-layers, --quantization-mode={gptq,awq,hybrid}.
- Telemetry keys to emit: quant.profile.id, quant.seed, per_layer_mse_{layer}, latency_p50/p95/p99, token_error_rate, embedding_cosine_drop.
- Provide a small compatibility shim to translate legacy 'weightonly' profile schema to new per-layer mapping (see internal PR linked below).
test_plan:
- Unit tests: profile loader round-trip for GPTQ/AWQ artifacts, mapping validation, schema roundtrip.
- Determinism test: run calibration twice with same seed/dataset; assert artifact hashes match.
- Regression harness: create 'golden' subset (100 prompts) and compute baseline outputs on FP32. Run WO-INT8 (GPTQ & AWQ) and assert metrics within thresholds.
- Stress test: run 10k short prompts in CI nightlies to detect flaky regressions.
- Canary test: staged rollout on staging cluster (5% traffic shadow), compare token-level diffs and embedding corpus cosine. If drift > configured SLO -> auto 0% traffic and open a rollback incident.
- Observability: dashboard tile with per-profile pass/fail, time-to-first-byte, and token error breakdown.
- Add regression-suite entry to nightly cron (runtime-1.21 branch).
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (Integration): merge profile loader + shim, enable local calibration, and store artifacts in s3 staging. Run deterministic tests.
Phase 2 (CI Canary): wire regression harness into PR gating on feature branches (non-blocking initially), generate PR comments with quick metrics.
Phase 3 (Shadow Canary): route 5% traffic as shadow runs against INT8 profiles (GPTQ/AWQ variants) and monitor drift metrics for 48h.
Phase 4 (Staged Traffic): if shadow stable, move to 20% staged traffic for 24h with auto-rollback.
Phase 5 (Full): enable as supported option for Dedicated customers with explicit opt-in and warn in Console.
Rollback conditions: any of the acceptance thresholds violated persistently for >5 minutes, or spike in token error rate > 4x baseline.
